tool_trace.content:
**Ranni the Witch** is an [NPC](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/NPCs "NPCs") in [Elden Ring](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Wiki "Elden Ring Wiki"). **Ranni the Witch** is a mysterious figure who first introduces herself as [Renna](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Renna "Renna"). Upon meeting her again at [Three Sisters](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Three_Sisters "Three Sisters"), she reveals her true name and eventually will recruit you into her servitude, sending you off in search of a hidden treasure. This page covers vital information for Ranni's questline for [Elden Ring](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Elden_Ring_Wiki "Elden Ring Wiki").

[See Ranni Lore](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ranni_the_Witch#lore)
> I am the witch Ranni. I stole Death long ago, and search now for the dark path.

Ranni is the daughter of [Radagon](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Radagon_of_the_Golden_Order "Radagon of the Golden Order") and [Rennala](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Rennala,_Queen_of_the_Full_Moon_(NPC) "Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (NPC)"), as such she is a princess of the [Carian Royal Family](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Carian_Royal_Family "Carian Royal Family"). After Radagon departed and became the consort to [Queen Marika](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Queen_Marika "Queen Marika"), Ranni and her siblings were raised to [demigod](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Demigods "Demigods") status, as they were now the children of the consort of a goddess. Unlike her siblings however, she was identified as a potential successor to Queen Marika by the Two Fingers, and her status was further elevated to that of an [Empyrean](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Empyrean "Empyrean"), and like Marika, granted her own shadow, [Blaidd](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blaidd "Blaidd").

She appears to have some involvement in The Night of Black Knives, where Black Knife Assassins stole a shard of the Rune of Death and murdered [Godwyn, the Golden](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Godwyn_the_Golden "Godwyn the Golden"). At the same time, Ranni seems to have lost her original body and now resides as a spirit inhabiting an artificial doll body. She now seeks a long-lost treasure with the aid of her loyal followers, [War Counselor Iji](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/War_Counselor_Iji "War Counselor Iji"), [Preceptor Seluvis](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Preceptor_Seluvis "Preceptor Seluvis"), her shadow [Blaidd](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blaidd "Blaidd"), and the Tarnished if they choose.

### Ranni the Witch Location in Elden Ring

Ranni the Witch can be found at [Ranni's Rise](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ranni%27s_Rise "Ranni's Rise") in the [Three Sisters](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Three_Sisters "Three Sisters") sub-region of [Liurnia of the Lakes](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Liurnia_of_the_Lakes "Liurnia of the Lakes") for a majority of Ranni's questline.

### Ranni Questline: How to Complete Ranni's Quest in Elden Ring

#### Ranni's Quest - First Meeting

- Ranni is first encountered going by the name [Renna](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Renna "Renna") when the player teleports or rests at the [Church of Elleh](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Church_of_Elleh "Church of Elleh") Site of Grace, after you have met [Melina](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Melina "Melina") and acquired [Torrent](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Torrent "Torrent").
- Once she has arrived, she will call out to the player to approach and speak with them. Upon doing so and answering her question in the affirmative, she will gift the player with the [Spirit Calling Bell](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Spirit_Calling_Bell "Spirit Calling Bell") and the [Lone Wolf Ashes](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Lone_Wolf_Ashes "Lone Wolf Ashes"). She will then disappear after being spoken to again, walking far enough away from her, or attempting to rest at the Site of Grace. [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67b6fa9240c157fd42bc83&markerId=465#tabber-Overland_Map "Interactive Map")

#### Ranni's Quest - Missed First Meeting

- If the player somehow misses their first encounter with Ranni, this will not prevent her quest from being completed. She can next be found in the [Liurnia](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Liurnia_of_the_Lakes "Liurnia of the Lakes") region, at the top of [Ranni's Rise](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ranni%27s_Rise "Ranni's Rise"). To access the area where Ranni's Rise resides, you must defeat [Royal Knight Loretta](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Royal_Knight_Loretta "Royal Knight Loretta") at the [Caria Manor](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Caria_Manor "Caria Manor").
- If her initial encounter is missed wherein the player receives the [Spirit Calling Bell](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Spirit_Calling_Bell "Spirit Calling Bell") and [Lone Wolf Ashes](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Lone_Wolf_Ashes "Lone Wolf Ashes") from Ranni, both can then be found and purchased from the [Twin Maiden Husks](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Twin_Maiden_Husks "Twin Maiden Husks") at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold").
- NOTE: Ranni will not appear in Ranni's Rise for the next step of her quest line if the Radahn Festival has already started at [Redmane Castle](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Redmane_Castle "Redmane Castle") (the Radahn Festival begins outside of Ranni's quest line progression if you have either activated the [Grand Lift of Dectus](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Grand_Lift_of_Dectus "Grand Lift of Dectus") or activated any Sites of Grace found within the [Altus Plateau](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Altus_Plateau "Altus Plateau")). This is because [Blaidd](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blaidd "Blaidd") is required to continue her quest line, and he will not leave the Radahn Festival until [Starscourge Radahn](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Starscourge_Radahn "Starscourge Radahn") has been defeated. Once Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, Ranni will reappear at Ranni's Rise and her quest line can be continued from then on.

#### Ranni's Quest - The Hidden Treasure of Nokron

- Ranni is later found in [Liurnia](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Liurnia "Liurnia") atop [Ranni's Rise](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ranni%27s_Rise "Ranni's Rise"). She tasks the player with finding the hidden treasure of [Nokron](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Nokron,_Eternal_City "Nokron, Eternal City") and asks that you speak with three people in her service: [War Counselor Iji](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/War_Counselor_Iji "War Counselor Iji"), Half-Wolf Warrior [Blaidd](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blaidd "Blaidd"), and Preceptor [Seluvis](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Seluvis "Seluvis"). The three will then appear as spectral projections within her tower that can be spoken with.
  - The player will be unable to leave the tower area until all three people have been spoken with and their dialogue exhausted (a fog wall barrier will physically block the player from leaving the area by foot/hoof and fast travel will be disabled). After speaking to the three, returning to Ranni and speaking with her will have her reveal that she is going to fall into a deep slumber soon and will not be able to speak with the player for some time. Once the player is finished speaking with Ranni, the player will be able to leave the area and fast travel again as normal.
  - Upon first meeting her at Ranni's Rise, if she tells you to begone after mentioning the curse mark on her discarded body and won't recruit you into her service, you will need to return to [Rogier](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Rogier "Rogier") at the [Roundtable Hold](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Roundtable_Hold "Roundtable Hold") and speak with him. He will suggest that you join into her service in order to learn more about where her curse mark could be found. You can then return to Ranni and speak with her to continue her quest line.
- Blaidd will be waiting in the [Siofra River](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Siofra_River "Siofra River") area [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67bad89240c157fd42bcf2&markerId=2799#tabber-Underground_Map "Interactive Map") (travel east from the Siofra River Bank Site of Grace until you reach the area where a Spirit Spring can be found, Blaidd will be standing nearby. However, be sure to defeat any enemies nearby as they can pursue you and cause issues with speaking with Blaidd). He will reveal that he suspects that [Preceptor Seluvis](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Preceptor_Seluvis "Preceptor Seluvis") knows more than he lets on and suggests that you go and speak with him. Upon speaking with Seluvis, he will inform you that [Sorceress Sellen](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Sorceress_Sellen "Sorceress Sellen") might have some information as to how to enter Nokron, and then provides you with [Seluvis's Introduction](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Seluvis%27s_Introduction "Seluvis's Introduction") to show her. Upon speaking with Sellen at the Waypoint Ruins [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67b6fa9240c157fd42bc83&markerId=707#tabber-Overland_Map "Interactive Map") and showing her Seluvis's Introduction, she informs the player that [Starscourge Radahn](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Starscourge_Radahn "Starscourge Radahn") has used his power to stop the movement of the stars, and that the only way to restore their movement and find an entrance into Nokron is to slay him.
  - NOTE: Informing Blaidd of what you've learned from Sellen concerning the stars and Radahn's actions will trigger the festival and temporarily alter the accessible layout of [Redmane Castle](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Redmane_Castle "Redmane Castle"), also potentially pausing certain NPC quests and interactions. Moreso, there have been cases where only talking to Sellen without talking to Blaidd afterwards also causes the festival to trigger.
  - Please note, if the player was unable to tolerate his "pleasant demeanor" and has killed Preceptor Seluvis, Blaidd will be hostile to you, and cause Ranni's quest line to halt until the player seeks Absolution at the Church of Vows.
  - Alternative ways to trigger the festival (and thus to kill Starscourge Radahn) are:
    - Accessing Altus Plateau, either via activating the Grand Lift of Dectus or through the Ruin-Strewn Precipice, will automatically trigger the festival on Redmane Castle.
    - The player can also access [Redmane Castle](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Redmane_Castle "Redmane Castle") earlier, talk to [Jerren](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Witch-Hunter_Jerren "Witch-Hunter Jerren") and tell him about [Iji](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/War_Counselor_Iji "War Counselor Iji"), which in turn will suggest you tell something to Iji. If the player then goes back to Iji and talks to him about Jerren, he will tell the player about going back to the festival, thus activating it. This can be done even if the player hasn't met Blaidd at Siofra River.
- Once Radahn has been slain, the stars will be freed to continue their flight, with one of them landing somewhere nearby. Returning to Iji and speaking with him reveals that the fallen star struck [Limgrave](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Limgrave "Limgrave") (the site is south of [Mistwood](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Mistwood "Mistwood"), fairly close to the ruins where the player could have first met Blaidd) and has created a new entrance into Nokron. Travelling to Limgrave, the landing site is hard to miss, as gravity magic from the fallen star has caused large chunks of rock to become permanently suspended in the air above the landing site. By carefully making their way down, the player can reach the city of Nokron. To reach the section of the city that holds the treasure Ranni wants, you must push through until you reach the Ancestral Woods Site of Grace [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67bad89240c157fd42bcf2&markerId=1580#tabber-Underground_Map "Interactive Map") and then jump across the nearby ledge and back into the city. Continue onward into the city and you will eventually find a treasure chest containing the [Fingerslayer Blade](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Fingerslayer_Blade "Fingerslayer Blade"), the secret treasure of Nokron that Ranni seeks.

#### Ranni's Quest - Releasing Ranni

- NOTE: Giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade will cause [Preceptor Seluvis](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Preceptor_Seluvis "Preceptor Seluvis") to become a lifeless puppet, which effectively locks you out of further interaction in his questline (And possibly prevents you from giving Seluvis' Potion to [Dung Eater](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Dung_Eater "Dung Eater")). If you want to get the [Magic Scorpion Charm](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Magic_Scorpion_Charm "Magic Scorpion Charm") from Seluvis in this playthrough, you need to start and/or continue through his quest line until he gifts the amulet to you, before giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade. After receiving the Magic Scorpion Charm, you may safely carry on with Ranni's quest line.
  - If Seluvis has given you the [Amber Draught](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Amber_Draught "Amber Draught") to give to Ranni at this point, once you have given her the Fingerslayer Blade you will no longer have the option to give the Amber Draught to Ranni.
    - However, don't be afraid of losing the option to give her the Amber Draught; As you aren't rewarded with anything for trying to give it to her, because it doesn't work on her and only serves to make her disappointed with you and halt her quest line until you seek Absolution at the [Church of Vows](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Church_of_Vows "Church of Vows").
- Upon returning to Ranni and giving her the Fingerslayer Blade, she will reward the player with the [Carian Inverted Statue](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Carian_Inverted_Statue "Carian Inverted Statue"), which they can use at the pedestal at the entrance to the [Carian Study Hall](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Carian_Study_Hall "Carian Study Hall") to reach the top of the Divine Tower of Liurnia. After speaking with her, Ranni will leave to continue her quest alone. Upon arriving at the top of the [Divine Tower of Liurnia](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Divine_Tower_of_Liurnia "Divine Tower of Liurnia"), you will be able to find the [Cursemark of Death](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Cursemark_of_Death "Cursemark of Death") upon the remains of Ranni's original body, which is severely burnt.  

[![rannis body elden ring wiki guide](https://static0.fextralifeimages.com/file/eldenring/c/c5/Rannis-body-elden-ring-wiki-guide.png)](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/File:Rannis-body-elden-ring-wiki-guide.png)

- After giving the Fingerslayer Blade to Ranni, you can speak with Iji, and he will tell you where Ranni has gone (mentioning Renna's Rise in the process) and the [Carian Filigreed Crest](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Carian_Filigreed_Crest "Carian Filigreed Crest") will be added to his merchant inventory for purchase, if you had yet to unlock its availability.
- At this point, the seal blocking access to [Renna's Rise](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Renna%27s_Rise "Renna's Rise") will have vanished, allowing access inside the tower. Upon reaching the top of the ladder within, you can find a chest containing the [Snow Witch Set](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Snow_Witch_Set "Snow Witch Set") that Ranni wore. Upon reaching the top of the tower, you can find a [waygate](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Waygates "Waygates") that will transport you to [Ainsel River Main](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ainsel_River_Main "Ainsel River Main"), where you can loot a [Miniature Ranni](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Miniature_Ranni "Miniature Ranni") doll nearby. After acquiring the doll, rest at the Ainsel River Main Site of Grace. [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67bad89240c157fd42bcf2&markerId=1963#tabber-Underground_Map "Interactive Map") You will see a new option listed amongst the others, that being "Talk to miniature Ranni." Select this option three times and Ranni will speak to you revealing that Ranni has possessed the doll. Annoyed at your interference, she will then task the player with defeating the [Baleful Shadow](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Baleful_Shadow "Baleful Shadow") found further into the area. The Baleful Shadow can be found just beyond the [Nokstella Waterfall Basin](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67bad89240c157fd42bcf2&markerId=2709#tabber-Underground_Map "Interactive Map") Site of Grace in [Nokstella, Eternal City](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Nokstella,_Eternal_City "Nokstella, Eternal City"). It is an agile and fairly strong opponent, so take caution when fighting it. After defeating the Baleful Shadow, Ranni will thank the player and reward them with the [Discarded Palace Key](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Discarded_Palace_Key "Discarded Palace Key"). Ranni will then say farewell as she still has things to do, her spirit leaving the doll.

#### Ranni's Quest - Returning to Ranni

- You are able to use the Discarded Palace Key to unlock the chest found in the [Raya Lucaria](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Raya_Lucaria_Academy "Raya Lucaria Academy") Grand Library next to [Rennala](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Rennala_Queen_of_the_Full_Moon "Rennala Queen of the Full Moon"). Inside you will find the [Dark Moon Ring](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Dark_Moon_Ring "Dark Moon Ring"). Once you have acquired the ring, travel back to the [Lake of Rot](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Lake_of_Rot "Lake of Rot") in the [Ainsel River](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ainsel_River "Ainsel River") area, and continue onward into the [Grand Cloister](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Grand_Cloister "Grand Cloister").
- By interacting with the stone coffin in the [Grand Cloister](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Grand_Cloister "Grand Cloister") [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67bad89240c157fd42bcf2&markerId=3003#tabber-Underground_Map "Interactive Map") (you can interact with it from a distance so that you do not have to stand in the Scarlet Rot water), the player can access a new area where they can find and defeat [Astel, Naturalborn of the Void](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Astel,_Naturalborn_of_the_Void "Astel, Naturalborn of the Void"). After its defeat, a new exit path can be traversed through (without having the Dark Moon Ring, an impassable magic seal blocks this exit). This path allows access to the southern-most section of Liurnia, the [Moonlight Altar](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Moonlight_Altar "Moonlight Altar"). Your next destination is the nearby [Cathedral of Manus Celes](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Cathedral_of_Manus_Celes "Cathedral of Manus Celes"). After collecting the 9 [Starlight Shards](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Starlight_Shards "Starlight Shards") inside scattered about and 1 outside near the stone object on the north side, drop down the hole near the Site of Grace and continue through the tunnel until you reach a recent battle site.
  - Please note, [Glintstone Dragon Adula](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Glintstone_Dragon_Adula "Glintstone Dragon Adula") will suddenly materialize near the [Cathedral of Manus Celes](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Cathedral_of_Manus_Celes "Cathedral of Manus Celes"), regardless of whether or not the dragon was forced to retreat at [Three Sisters](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Three_Sisters "Three Sisters"), so take caution when exploring the area.
- Interact with Ranni's doll body to place the Dark Moon Ring on Ranni's finger. Her doll body will then disappear and Ranni, fully restored to her previous life-sized doll form, will appear and thank the player. She confirms that the player is now her consort and promises that they will meet again. After Ranni vanishes, an item will appear where she once stood. Loot the item to acquire the [Dark Moon Greatsword](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Dark_Moon_Greatsword "Dark Moon Greatsword").
- Provided Ranni's quest line has been completed; after defeating the Elden Beast, a blue summon sign will appear on the ground near Marika's broken remains. The player can interact with this summon sign (instead of interacting with Marika's remains) to acquire the ["Age of the Stars" ending](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Endings "Endings"). Doing so will also unlock a related game achievement/trophy.

### Elden Ring Ranni the Witch Notes & Trivia

- Ranni's body was willingly slain along with Godwyn's soul (unwillingly) on the Night of the Black Knives, leading to Ranni binding her soul to a life-sized doll, modeled in the likeness of her former mentor described as "the snowy crone" (see [Snow Witch Robe](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Snow_Witch_Robe "Snow Witch Robe")). As seen on her body, she had also inherited the red hair of her father, Radagon of the Golden Order.
- After completing her quest line, a new [Site of Grace](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Site_of_Grace "Site of Grace") called "Ranni's Chamber" will appear at the top of Ranni's Rise. [Map Link](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Interactive_Map?mapId=vm6a67b6fa9240c157fd42bc83&markerId=1807#tabber-Overland_Map "Interactive Map") While resting at that Site of Grace, you have the option to speak to the [Miniature Ranni](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Miniature_Ranni "Miniature Ranni"). Doing so will have Ranni's spirit explain the details of her plan and her intentions for the world. Hearing this dialogue will change the way Ranni addresses you in the Age of Stars ending, from "**Fair** Consort" to "**Dear** Consort".
- Some speculate that Ranni and Melina have some sort of close connection, as both are spirits who lost their former bodies and both have opposing eye seals, a trait not seen on most other characters. However, given that Ranni's current doll body (and thus perhaps her eye seal) is based on her former mentor, the old snow witch, it might be that the old snow witch is the one with a connection to Melina, not Ranni.
- Ranni's doll body shares a similarity with the [Marionette Soldier](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Marionette_Soldier "Marionette Soldier") enemies found throughout the Lands Between that appear to also have come from Liurnia, in that they both were built to have four arms.
- If Ranni is attacked after giving her Dark Moon Ring in front of the slayed two finger, she will have a protective barrier, give some dialogue about it being what she deserved for surrounding herself with delusions and then disappear. ([Blaidd](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blaidd "Blaidd") will still appear feral and you will be able to obtain his armor and weapon). Using [Celestial Dew](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Celestial_Dew "Celestial Dew") to atone, will bring Ranni back to her position below the Church (in front of the slain two fingers).
- It appears that Ranni's Great Rune is etched upon the surface of the moon. Gideon says that Ranni had cast aside her Great Rune, and the symbol appearing on the moon would likely be where she had placed it.
- Ranni likely had a close connection (besides being siblings) with [Praetor Rykard](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Rykard,_Lord_of_Blasphemy "Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy") at some point in the past, given part of the description of the [Blasphemous Claw](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Blasphemous_Claw "Blasphemous Claw") item "On the night of the dire plot, Ranni rewarded Praetor Rykard with these traces. Should the coming trespass one day transpire, they would serve as a last-resort foil, allowing Rykard to challenge Maliketh the Black Blade, the black beast of Destined Death."
- If you attack Ranni or her Allies at all before she falls into her slumber, Ranni will no longer become available to you at [Ranni's Rise](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Ranni%27s_Rise "Ranni's Rise"). Using [Celestial Dew](https://eldenring.wiki.fextralife.com/Celestial_Dew "Celestial Dew") to atone will bring Ranni back to her place.

# [2401.07883] The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator

[View PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.07883) [HTML (experimental)](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.07883v1)
> Abstract:Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has become one of the most popular paradigms for enabling LLMs to access external data, and also as a mechanism for grounding to mitigate against hallucinations. When implementing RAG you can face several challenges like effective integration of retrieval models, efficient representation learning, data diversity, computational efficiency optimization, evaluation, and quality of text generation. Given all these challenges, every day a new technique to improve RAG appears, making it unfeasible to experiment with all combinations for your problem. # The Chronicles of RAG: The Retriever, the Chunk and the Generator

## Abstract

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) has become one of the most popular paradigms for enabling LLMs to access external data, and also as a mechanism for grounding to mitigate against hallucinations. When implementing RAG you can face several challenges like effective integration of retrieval models, efficient representation learning, data diversity, computational efficiency optimization, evaluation, and quality of text generation. Given all these challenges, every day a new technique to improve RAG appears, making it unfeasible to experiment with all combinations for your problem. In this context, this paper presents good practices to implement, optimize, and evaluate RAG for the Brazilian Portuguese language, focusing on the establishment of a simple pipeline for inference and experiments. We explored a diverse set of methods to answer questions about the first Harry Potter book. To generate the answers we used the OpenAI's gpt-4, gpt-4-1106-preview, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, and Google's Gemini Pro. Focusing on the quality of the retriever, our approach achieved an improvement of MRR@10 by 35.4% compared to the baseline. When optimizing the input size in the application, we observed that it is possible to further enhance it by 2.4%. Finally, we present the complete architecture of the RAG with our recommendations. As result, we moved from a baseline of 57.88% to a maximum relative score of 98.61%.

## AI Overview

Our new overview generator adds more detail and page citations

## Overview

This paper presents a comprehensive empirical study of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems specifically tailored for Brazilian Portuguese, addressing a critical gap in non-English RAG research. The authors systematically evaluate various RAG components to establish "good practices" for building effective Portuguese-language RAG systems, using the first Harry Potter book as their test corpus.

![Figure 1: Data preparation workflow showing the conversion of book text into chunks and question-answer pairs](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-0.jpeg "Figure 1: Data preparation workflow showing the conversion of book text into chunks and question-answer pairs")

## Problem Statement and Motivation

RAG systems have emerged as a crucial solution to address limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly their tendency to generate outdated information and their lack of access to external or domain-specific knowledge. However, the rapidly evolving RAG landscape presents significant challenges for practitioners who cannot feasibly test every new technique for their specific use cases.

The authors identify several key problems:

- The overwhelming proliferation of RAG techniques makes it difficult to select optimal configurations
- Most RAG research focuses on English, leaving other languages underexplored
- RAG system quality heavily depends on retriever effectiveness
- There's a lack of practical, validated guidelines for implementing RAG in non-English contexts

## Methodology and Experimental Design

### Data Preparation and Evaluation Framework

The researchers used the first Harry Potter book in Brazilian Portuguese, dividing it into 140 non-overlapping chunks of 1000 tokens each. For each chunk, they generated question-answer pairs using GPT-4, ensuring answers were directly extractable from the reference text to mirror the SQuAD dataset format.

A key methodological innovation is their custom evaluation approach. Recognizing limitations of traditional metrics like BLEU and ROUGE for contextual similarity, they developed a GPT-4-based scoring system using a 5-point scale (1, 3, 5, 7, 10). They introduced the concept of a "relative maximum score" - the average performance when LLMs evaluate correct {question, chunk} pairs - establishing a realistic upper bound of approximately 7.4 out of 10.

All results are reported as "degradation scores" calculated as:

<!-- MathML: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mtext>Degradation Score</mtext><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mtext>Experiment Score</mtext><mtext>Relative Maximum</mtext></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{Degradation Score} = 1 - \frac{\text{Experiment Score}}{\text{Relative Maximum}}</annotation></semantics></math> --> Degradation Score=1−Experiment ScoreRelative Maximum\text{Degradation Score} = 1 - \frac{\text{Experiment Score}}{\text{Relative Maximum}}

### Experimental Architecture

The study progressed through baseline experiments to advanced retriever optimizations:

**Baseline Experiments:**

- **No Context:** Testing LLMs without any retrieved information
- **Long Context:** Evaluating GPT-4-1106-preview with the entire book as context to identify "Lost in The Middle" effects
- **RAG Naive:** Basic RAG pipeline using ADA-002 embeddings with default parameters

**Advanced Retriever Evaluation:** The core methodology involved systematic comparison of retrieval strategies using Recall@k and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR@k) metrics:

1. **Sparse Retrieval (BM25):** Comparing Pyserini BM25 (with Portuguese-specific preprocessing) against basic rank-bm25
2. **Dense Retrieval (ADA-002):** Using OpenAI's embedding model in a bi-encoder setup
3. **Custom Embedding:** Fine-tuning ADA-002 using Mean Squared Error loss with positive and negative examples from the dataset
4. **Hybrid Search:** Combining sparse and dense retrievers using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
5. **Multi-stage Reranking:** Using BM25 for initial retrieval followed by cross-encoder reranking with unicamp-dl/mt5-base-en-pt-msmarco-v2

## Key Findings and Results

### Retriever Quality is Paramount

The study's most significant finding is that retriever quality directly correlates with overall RAG performance. The multi-stage reranking approach achieved the best retrieval metrics with an MRR@10 of 0.919 and perfect Recall@9 of 1.0, representing a 35.4% improvement over baseline ADA-002.

![Figure 2: Performance comparison across different retrieval methods showing degradation scores vs. MRR@10](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-11.jpeg "Figure 2: Performance comparison across different retrieval methods showing degradation scores vs. MRR@10")

### Context Length Optimization

Despite achieving perfect recall with 9 chunks, optimal RAG performance occurred when retrieving only 3 chunks. This finding confirms that more context doesn't necessarily improve performance and can even degrade it due to the "Lost in The Middle" phenomenon.

![Figure 3: Lost in The Middle effect showing performance degradation based on answer position in long context](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-2.jpeg "Figure 3: Lost in The Middle effect showing performance degradation based on answer position in long context")

### Language-Specific Improvements

The custom fine-tuned ADA-002 embedding showed substantial improvements for Portuguese text, achieving better separation between positive and negative examples in the embedding space:

![Figure 4: Cosine similarity distribution comparison between standard and custom ADA-002 embeddings](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-5.jpeg "Figure 4: Cosine similarity distribution comparison between standard and custom ADA-002 embeddings")

The fine-tuning process improved the model's ability to distinguish relevant from irrelevant content, with positive examples clustering at higher similarity scores.

### Final Performance Results

The optimal configuration (BM25 + Reranker with 3 chunks) achieved 98.61% relative accuracy, representing only -1.4% degradation from the theoretical maximum. This configuration improved performance by 40.73 percentage points compared to the no-context baseline.

![Figure 5: Progressive improvement in accuracy across different RAG configurations](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-13.jpeg "Figure 5: Progressive improvement in accuracy across different RAG configurations")

Notably, under optimal RAG conditions, Gemini Pro achieved performance comparable to GPT-4 (-2.2% vs. -1.4% degradation), suggesting its viability for Portuguese RAG applications.

## Technical Architecture Details

### Hybrid Search Implementation

The hybrid approach combines BM25 and dense retrieval using Reciprocal Rank Fusion:

![Figure 6: RRF algorithm combining rankings from different retrievers](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-7.jpeg "Figure 6: RRF algorithm combining rankings from different retrievers")

For each document, RRF calculates:

<!-- MathML: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"><semantics><mrow><mtext>RRF Score</mtext><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mtext>rank</mtext><mtext>BM25</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msub><mtext>rank</mtext><mtext>dense</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\text{RRF Score} = \frac{1}{\text{rank}_{\text{BM25}} + k} + \frac{1}{\text{rank}_{\text{dense}} + k}</annotation></semantics></math> --> RRF Score=1rankBM25+k+1rankdense+k\text{RRF Score} = \frac{1}{\text{rank}_{\text{BM25}} + k} + \frac{1}{\text{rank}_{\text{dense}} + k}

where k=1 in their implementation.

### Multi-stage Reranking Pipeline

The best-performing configuration employed a two-stage approach:

![Figure 7: Multi-stage reranking architecture](https://paper-assets.alphaxiv.org/figures/2401.07883v1/img-8.jpeg "Figure 7: Multi-stage reranking architecture")

1. BM25 retrieves 50 candidate documents
2. Cross-encoder reranker (unicamp-dl/mt5-base-en-pt-msmarco-v2) scores and reorders candidates
3. Top-k documents are selected for the LLM

The reranker uses a T5-based architecture that processes query-document pairs jointly, providing more nuanced relevance scoring than bi-encoder approaches.

## Significance and Impact

This research provides valuable practical guidance for implementing RAG systems in Brazilian Portuguese, addressing a significant gap in multilingual AI research. The systematic evaluation methodology and introduction of the "relative maximum score" concept offers a robust framework for future RAG evaluations.

Key contributions include:

1. **Language-specific insights:** Demonstrating that Portuguese-specific preprocessing and fine-tuning significantly improve retrieval quality
2. **Practical architecture recommendations:** Establishing that multi-stage reranking with optimal chunk count provides the best performance
3. **Evaluation methodology:** Introducing degradation scores relative to achievable maxima provides more meaningful performance comparisons
4. **Resource optimization:** Showing that 3 chunks provide optimal performance despite perfect recall at 9 chunks, offering computational efficiency gains

The work emphasizes that effective RAG implementation requires careful consideration of retriever quality, context management, and language-specific optimizations. The finding that sophisticated retrieval strategies can enable smaller models like Gemini Pro to achieve GPT-4-level performance in optimized RAG settings has important implications for cost-effective deployment of multilingual AI systems.

This study serves as both a practical guide for Portuguese RAG implementation and a methodological template for evaluating RAG systems in other languages, contributing to the broader goal of democratizing advanced AI capabilities across linguistic boundaries.

Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive nlp tasks

This is the seminal paper that introduced the Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework. It is fundamental to the main paper as it defines the core concept and technology being implemented, analyzed, and optimized.

[2] P. Lewis, E. Perez, A. Piktus, F. Petroni, V. Karpukhin, N. Goyal, H. Küttler, M. Lewis, W. tau Yih, T. Rock-täschel, S. Riedel, and D. Kiela, “Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive nlp tasks,” 2021.

Lost in the middle: How language models use long contexts

This paper is heavily referenced and its findings are directly tested in the 'Long Context' section of the main paper. It provides the basis for understanding why RAG performance degrades with larger input sizes and specific answer positioning, a key experimental result.

[17] N. F. Liu, K. Lin, J. Hewitt, A. Paranjape, M. Bevilacqua, F. Petroni, and P. Liang, “Lost in the middle: How language models use long contexts,” 2023.

G-eval: Nlg evaluation using gpt-4 with better human alignment

The evaluation methodology of the entire study is based on the concept from this paper, using gpt-4 to score the quality of generated answers. This citation is critical as it underpins how the performance of all tested RAG configurations is measured and compared.

[9] Y. Liu, D. Iter, Y. Xu, S. Wang, R. Xu, and C. Zhu, “G-eval: Nlg evaluation using gpt-4 with better human alignment,” 2023.

[Multi-stage document ranking with BERT](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/1910.14424)

This paper is cited as introducing the concept of multi-stage ranking with transformer models, specifically the reranker pipeline. This is highly relevant because the main paper's experiments conclude that a multi-stage architecture with a reranker achieves the best overall performance.

[28] R. F. Nogueira, W. Yang, K. Cho, and J. Lin, “Multi-stage document ranking with BERT,” CoRR, vol. abs/1910.14424, 2019. [Online]. Available: http://arxiv.org/abs/1910.14424

1

Introduction

The rise of Large Language Models (LLMs) has changed the way we approach Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications.  
Their ability to answer different user queries in different domains allow these models to show a notable performance  
in a wide range of tasks like translation, summarizing, question answering, and many others [\[1\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)However, there are  
a lot of open challenges when it comes to problems that require answers based on updated information, and external  
data, that were not available in the training data.

In order to overcome this challenge, a technique called Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) [\[2\] ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)was developed.  
This approach aims to solve the limitation of the need for external data, by fetching and incorporating this information  
in the prompt. With this, the model can generate more cohesive answers about subjects and data not seen during the  
training, decreasing the occurrence of hallucinations [\[3\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)Nevertheless, this approach adds a new layer of challenges  
since it requires the development of a trustworthy retriever pipeline, given that the quality of the final answer can be  
highly affected if the retrieved text is not relevant to the user query [\[4\].](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)

The landscape of RAG is rapidly expanding, with a constant influx of new papers introducing diverse implementations  
[\[5\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)Each of these variants proposes technical modifications or enhancements, such as different retrieval mechanisms,  
augmentation techniques, or fine-tuning methodologies. This proliferation, while a testament to the field’s dynamism,

PREPRINT

presents a substantial challenge for AI practitioners. The task of methodically experimenting with, and critically  
evaluating, each variant’s performance, scalability, and applicability becomes increasingly complex.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive series of experiments focused on the application of RAG specifically tailored  
for Brazilian Portuguese. Our research delves into evaluating various retrieval techniques, including both sparse and  
dense retrievers. Additionally, we explore two chunking strategies (naive and sentence window) to optimize the  
integration of retrieved information into the generation process. We also investigate the impact of the positioning of  
documents within the prompt, analyzing how this influences the overall quality and relevance of the generated content.  
Finally, our experiments extend to comparing the performance of different LLMs, notably GPT-4 and Gemini, in their  
ability to effectively incorporate the retrieved information and produce coherent, contextually accurate responses. This  
paper aims to provide valuable insights and practical guidelines for implementing RAG in Brazilian Portuguese.

Our main contributions are summarized as follows: 1) we propose a methodology to prepare a dataset in a format that  
allows quantifying the quality of the different steps in an RAG system. 2) We proposed a metric (maximum relative  
score) that allow us to direct quantify the existent gap between each approach and a perfect RAG system. 3) We discuss  
and compare different implementations, showing good practices and optimizations that can be used when developing  
a RAG system.

2

Data Preparation

The chosen dataset was the first Harry Potter book in its Brazilian Portuguese version. This choice is motivated

5

Advanced Experiments

The studies and experiments outlined in section [4 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#3)have shown unsatisfactory performance, marked by a degradation  
of at least 20% compared to the peak relative performance. Therefore, in this section, we explore various retrieval  
approaches for the RAG, recognizing that the quality of the retriever is a crucial factor in enhancing performance for  
this type of problem. We conducted an evaluation covering both sparse and dense search, a hybrid method, and even  
a multi-stage architecture using a reranker.

In pursuit of code debugging flexibility and easier customization at each stage, we chose not to utilize an RAG frame-  
work (like LangChain or Llama-Index). For a comprehensive guide on debugging RAG and more details about retrieval  
systems, refer to [\[20\] ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)and [\[21\].](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)

5.1

Retrievers

When deploying retrieval systems, it is essential to achieve a balance between “effectiveness” (How good are the  
results returned?

) and “efficiency” (How much time it takes to return the results? or How much resources are used in

terms of disk/RAM/GPU?

). This balance ensures that latency, result quality, and computational budget remain within

our application’s required limits. This work will exclusively focus on effectiveness measures to quantify the retrievers  
methods quality.

In our retriever experiments, the evaluation strategy centers around assessing how well the retriever performs in re-  
trieving relevant information based on each given query qi. To achieve this, we employ the concept of recall. It is  
defined as the fraction of the relevant documents for a given query qi that are successfully retrieved in a ranked list  
R [\[21\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)This metric is based on binary relevance judgments, assuming that documents are either relevant or not [\[21\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)In this paper, each chunk is considered a document and only the respective chunk di is considered relevant to the query  
qi. While recall is easy to interpret, it does not consider the specific rank positions in which the relevant chunk appears  
in R.

To overcome this limitation, we introduce Reciprocal Rank (RR) into our analysis. In this metric, the rank of the  
first relevant document to the query in R is used to compute the RR score [\[21\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)Therefore, Reciprocal Rank offers a  
more nuanced evaluation by assigning a higher value when the relevant chunk is returned in the early positions of our  
retrievers given the respective query.

Recall and Reciprocal Rank were evaluated at a specific cutoff so the measures are presented as R@k and MRR@k.  
For each query, its results are evaluated and their mean serves as an aggregated measure of effectiveness of a given  
retriever method. The retrievers are introduced below.

In the category of sparse retrievers, we emphasize the BM25, a technique grounded in statistical weighting to assess  
relevance between search terms and documents. BM25 employs a scoring function that takes into account term  
frequency and document length, offering an efficient approach for retrieving pertinent information and is typically  
used as a strong baseline. However, it is exact-match based and can be powerless when query and document are  
relevant to each other but has no common words.

On the other hand, when exploring dense retrievers, we often encounter approaches based on the called bi-encoder  
design [\[22\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)The bi-encoder independently encodes queries and documents, creating separate vector representations  
before calculating similarity. An advantage of this approach is that it can be initialized ‘offline’: document embeddings  
can be precomputed, leaving only the query embedding being calculated at search time, reducing latency.

The hybrid search technique aims to leverage the best of both sparse and dense search approaches. Given a question,  
both searches are conducted in parallel, generating two lists of candidate documents to answer it. The challenge then  
lies in combining the two results in the best possible way, ensuring that the final hybrid list surpasses the individual  
searches. Essentially, we can conceptualize it as a voting system, where each searcher casts a vote on the relevance of  
a document to a given query, and in the end, the opinions are combined to produce a better result.

The multi-stage search architecture is based on the retrieve-and-rerank pipeline. In the first stage, a retriever with good  
recall is typically used to perform an initial filtering of the documents to be returned. From this narrowed-down list,  
these candidate documents are then sent to a second stage, which involves higher computational complexity, to rerank  
them and enhance the final effectiveness of the system.

Next, we provide more details about each retriever used.

The hyperparameters that exert the most significant impact on performance include the learning rate, batch size, and  
the number of dimensions in the projection matrix. The ADA-002 model has 1536 dimensions, and the projection  
matrix is of size 1536 × N, where N ∈ 1024, 2048, 4096\. In our experiments, we observed that 2048 dimensions  
resulted in the best accuracy.

This type of fine-tuning requires low GPU resources, with a training time of approximately 5 minutes using the A100  
GPU. The model itself is straightforward, consisting of a matrix with dropout (to mitigate overfitting), followed by the  
hyperbolic tangent activation function, which provided additional accuracy gains in the training set.

Reranker

The fundamental idea underlying multi-stage ranking is to divide document ranking into a sequence of stages. After  
an initial retrieval, which usually involves a sparse retriever or dense retriever, each subsequent stage re-evaluates and  
reranks the set of candidates forwarded from the preceding stage. Figure [9 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#9)represents a multi-stage pipeline where  
Pyserini BM25 performs the first stage and the candidate chunks are then re-evaluated by the reranker. After that, the  
final reranked list called retrieved chunks is presented as final result formed by k chunks.

The initial utilization of transformers within a multi-stage ranking framework was presented in the study [\[28\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)Their  
proposed model, known as monoBERT, transforms the ranking process into a relevance classification problem. It  
achieves this by sorting texts based on the conditional probability P (Relevant = 1 | di; q), where q is the query and  
di represents documents [\[21\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)The model simultaneously processes both queries and documents. This simultaneous  
processing leads to a more enriched interaction between them, often resulting in improved effectiveness [\[29\], \[30\]. ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)However, this neural models have a substantial number of parameters and the scoring of query-document pairs occurs  
at inference time. This, in turn, increases computational costs and latency. This kind of model is also known by  
cross-encoder. Refer to Figure [10 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#10)for an illustration of the query-document pair processing.

Figure 10: Cross-Encoder

In the other hand, monoT5 is a sequence-to-sequence reranker [\[31\] ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)that uses T5 models [\[32\] ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)to generate relevance  
scores between a pair of query and document. T5 models treat all tasks as text-to-text, requiring some adaptations  
for the query/document similarity task. During training, the format

'Query: {query} Document: {document}

Relevant:' is used, with labels yes if the document is relevant to the query, and no otherwise. At inference time, the  
same format as the training data is used to format pairs of queries and documents to feed the model, and a single-token  
greedy decode is performed. The score is then obtained by calculating the softmax value considering only the tokens

no and yes, and selecting the value corresponding to the yes token. Note that the tokens no and yes are the tokens  
used in the version provided by [\[33\], ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)but the publication that introduced the monoT5 architecture, [\[31\], ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)uses the tokens

false and true. Figure [11 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#10)contains an illustration of the monoT5 architecture’s inference process.

Figure 11: monoT5’s inference process

In our experiments, Pyserini BM25 was employed as first-stage retrieval, retrieving 50 documents to be reranked in the  
second stage. In the second stage, we utilized the model

unicamp-dl/mt5-base-en-pt-msmarco-v2, a sequence-

to-sequence reranker trained on pairs of queries and documents in English and Portuguese from the dataset [\[33\].](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#14)

6

Conclusions

The implementation of RAG systems faces challenges such as the effective integration of retrieval models, efficient  
representation learning, the diversity of data, the optimization of computational efficiency, evaluation, and text genera-  
tion quality. Faced with these constantly evolving obstacles, this article proposes best practices for the implementation,  
optimization, and evaluation of RAG on a Brazilian Portuguese dataset, focusing on a simplified pipeline for inference  
and experimentation.

So far, we have introduced the main components and methods along with their results and gaps. In this section, we will  
discuss key points that contribute to the performance improvement in RAG applications. We will start by discussing  
the relationship between the quality of the retriever and the achieved performance, in which our approach showed  
a significant improvement of MRR@10 by 35.4% compared to the baseline. Next, we will address the impact of  
input size on performance. In this domain, we observed that it is possible to enhance the best information retrieval  
strategy by 2.4% through input size optimization. Finally, we will present the complete architecture of RAG with  
our recommendations. When evaluating the final accuracy of our approach, we reached 98.61%, representing an  
improvement of 40.73 in less degradation score compared to the baseline.

6.3

Final Results

Despite this work being grounded in a single dataset, it is always crucial to emphasize the importance of data quality.  
In a simplified manner, as illustrated in Figure [13, ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#12)data quality in RAG can be divided into Input, Retriever, and  
Evaluation.

Figure 13: Core Points in RAG.

• Input: How are the queries formulated? Are they synthetic or generic? What is the application’s purpose?

Building a RAG for a chatbot differs significantly from constructing a RAG for extracting information from  
a long and complex document.

• Retriever: How do the data behave in information retrieval? Are the queries strongly linked by keywords in

the text? What is the cosine similarity of query-to-query, query-to-document, and document-to-document?

• Evaluation: How are the data measured? Defining metrics and success rates, as in the first experiment, is

always a safe path to avoid biases. Build the evaluation system before testing, avoiding bias.

In conclusion, the main contribution of this work was to identify and present the best possible configuration of tech-  
niques and parameters for a RAG application. Figure [14 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#13)provides a summarized overview of the end-to-end experi-  
ment results for the discussed approaches, and the best practices recommended by this study achieve a final accuracy  
of 98.61%, representing an improvement of 40.73 percentage points compared to the baseline.

B

Sentence Window

There are a wide variety of techniques available for dealing with RAG and new approaches are constantly emerging. In  
this work we highlight the main existing strategies, although we have also explored others, such as the RAG Sentence  
Window approach.

The sentence window chunk constitutes a strategy embedded in the llama-inde[x1, ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#16)which employs the small-to-large  
approach. The entire chunk retrieval process is based on cosine similarity. Initially, a single sentence is retrieved,  
followed by expanding (window) around the retrieved sentence to construct a more extensive chunk. This method  
implies that the most relevant context is always centered and retrieved first, as opposed to being at the edges of a  
chunk boundary. Figure [15 ](1793420529076-0ee7db82-e7c4-4323-bded-e77fb672f3c2-file10865.html#16)illustrates the comparison between naive chunks and those obtained through the "sentence  
window" strategy.

Figure 15: Comparison between the naive chunking and small to big strategies, where the latter initially retrieves a  
single sentence and then performs windowing with padding on both sides.
